peek's MCP server

peek keeps the images, videos and audio an agent makes on its host, and serves each back by a link that plays in the person's browser. Its MCP server is for agents: upload a file, by its /cellar/peek/ path where the agent has the shared drive, else small ones inline and large ones by a single-use upload URL that curl sends from the shell, and give the person its link; find, change and delete what was uploaded. It is served at /mcp (streamable HTTP, stateless, answering JSON), under a token from peek token create <name>; each tool is one API request made with it, so it is refused and answered as that request would be. A refusal comes back as the tool's error, in the API's words. The contract is mcp.json; the API's is here.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "peek": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://peek.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <your token>"
      }
    }
  }
}

Instructions

What the server tells an agent when it connects:

peek: See what your agents made, wherever you are. It keeps the images, videos and audio you make, on this host, and gives each a link that shows or plays it in the person's browser, on their phone too. Upload a screenshot, a screen recording or a sound you want the person to see or hear, and give them its link (in a PR, a task comment or a message) instead of attaching the file. - On a host with /cellar (the shared drive), the fast way to upload is to write the file under /cellar/peek/ and pass its path to upload_asset: peek records it without copying, from any host, and the asset shows as pending until its file has reached peek's host, then plays. Prefer it to content or an upload URL wherever you can write there. - upload_asset takes the file's name and what it is for: repo (owner/name) and pr, task (a waypoint short id), title, tags. Otherwise give content (the file in base64) only for a small file, up to a few MB. For anything larger, give no content: it answers an uploadUrl and the exact curl command to run in your shell, which needs no token and works once, within the hour. Either way it answers the asset's link. - Give the person link, never fileUrl: link is the page that plays it. - list_assets finds what was uploaded, newest first, by repo, pr, task, tags, contentType prefix (video/), createdBy or text in q; pass nextToken for the next page. - update_asset changes what an asset is of; delete_asset removes it and its file. - Every tool takes the token this server was connected with.

Tools

  • upload_asset Upload an asset
  • list_assets List assets
  • get_asset Get an asset
  • update_asset Update an asset
  • delete_asset Delete an asset

upload_asset

Keeps a file and answers its link, the page that shows or plays it, to give the person. With path (a file you wrote under /cellar/peek/) it is recorded in place, never copied: the fastest way where you have /cellar. With content (base64, for a small file) it is stored now and the asset answered. Without it, answers an uploadUrl and the curl command that uploads the file from your shell: run it with <file> replaced by the file's path. It needs no token, works once within the hour, and answers the asset; the link answered now works once it has run.

InputTypeRequired
namestringThe file's name, with its extension: no path. Required unless path is given, whose last part it defaults to.
contentTypestringIts media type, such as video/mp4. Default: the name's extension's.
titlestringWhat it shows, in a few words.
descriptionstringMore on what it shows, or what to look for.
repostringThe GitHub repository it is for, as owner/name.
printegerThe pull request it is for, in repo.
taskstringThe waypoint task it is for, by its short id.
tagsstring[]Tags, at most 20.
pathstringThe file's absolute path under /cellar/peek, written there on any host with /cellar: peek serves it in place, never copying it, and it is pending until it reaches peek's host. The fastest way to upload where you can write there; leave out content.
contentstringThe file, in base64, for a small one (at most 16,000,000 characters, about 12 MB). Leave it out to be given an uploadUrl and a curl command that uploads the file from your shell instead.

list_assets reads only

Assets matching every filter given, newest first, a page at a time: while nextToken is not null, pass it for the next page.

InputTypeRequired
repostringOnly those for this repository.
prnumberOnly those for this pull request.
taskstringOnly those for this waypoint task.
tagsstring[]Only those carrying every one of these tags.
contentTypestringOnly those whose media type starts with this, such as video/ or image/png.
createdBystringOnly those uploaded by this caller.
qstringOnly those whose name, title or description holds this text, ignoring case.
maxResultsintegerThe most to answer. Default: 50.
nextTokenstringThe nextToken a page answered, for the page after it.

get_asset reads only

An asset, with its link and fileUrl.

InputTypeRequired
idstringyesThe asset's id: 12 URL-safe characters.

update_asset

Sets what an asset is of: the fields given, leaving the rest. Its bytes and name do not change.

InputTypeRequired
idstringyesThe asset's id: 12 URL-safe characters.
titlestring or nullWhat it shows, in a few words; null clears it.
descriptionstring or nullMore on what it shows; null clears it.
repostring or nullThe repository it is for, as owner/name; null clears it.
printeger or nullThe pull request it is for; null clears it.
taskstring or nullThe waypoint task it is for; null clears it.
tagsstring[]Its tags, replacing those it had.

delete_asset

Removes the asset from the catalog, then its file. Its link and file URL answer 404 after.

InputTypeRequired
idstringyesThe asset's id: 12 URL-safe characters.
